title: Gemini Lab Call Record
description: RESEARCH-ONLY record of exactly one call to the Gemini API, or of exactly one refusal to make it. Written under research/rehearsals/provider-labs/gemini-vlm/runs/ and nowhere else. Never a production write, never read by production code. Two rules the schema enforces rather than trusts: identity is explicit (`mode` distinguishes live from replay from fixture, and cannot be inferred), and telemetry that was not observed is null. An absent RPM is `null`, never a number copied from an article.

mode.description: Which transport was configured — never inferred, never merged. live = the live HTTP transport; replay = a frozen record read back through a transport that RAISES if anything reaches for the network; fixture = a scripted fake, used by the test suite. Note that `live` names the transport, not the event: a record whose outcome.status is `unavailable` was configured live and never used it, because there was no key.

endpoint.description: Path only. The API key travels in the x-goog-api-key header and MUST NOT appear here.

prompt_id.description: id from prompts.json, when a canonical prompt was used

image_parts.description: What was sent, by digest. Bytes are never written into the record.

outcome.description: Exactly one of these five. `empty` and `refused` are results, not failures, and are never collapsed into `error`.

error_message.description: Redacted. The key is scrubbed before this is written.

telemetry.description: Observed only. Every field is nullable and null MEANS the API did not report it.

epistemic.description: The whole reason this lab is a lab. A VLM's answer about an image is INTERPRETIVE until some capability measures the distinction it names. Nothing here may claim otherwise, and `measured` is fixed false by the schema — a record that wanted it true would have to change this file, which is the review that ought to happen.

corpus_invariant.description: Source-post fingerprints before and after the call. Rule 10: the posts are read, never written.
